description_full: Vinci SA, together with its subsidiaries, engages in concessions, energy, and construction businesses in France and internationally. It operates through Concessions, Energy Solutions, and Construction segments. The company's Concessions segment operates motorways, autoroutes, airports, highways, railways, and stadiums. Its Energy segment provides services to the manufacturing sector, infrastructure, building solutions and facilities management, and information and communication technology; and industrial and energy-related services, which includes development of renewable energy assets, as well as engineering, procurement, construction projects in the energy sector, and development of renewable energy production facilities of solar, and wind farms. The company's Construction segment engages in designing and undertaking projects, which includes general contractor; geotechnical, and structural engineering and related digital activities, as well as provision of services in nuclear engineering; undertaking building, civil engineering, roadworks, rail works, and water works; development of properties, including residential and commercial properties; and management of residences and property services. Vinci SA was founded in 1899 and is headquartered in Nanterre, France.

financial_summary: Vinci SA is a large-cap industrials business with a $67.9B market cap on $82.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 15% against a 7% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 57% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $8.8B in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.42× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sector_headwinds.text: Altman Z in the distress zone (1.1) — the kind of balance-sheet risk that can make a loss permanent

Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.

ROE of 16% is amplified by 4.3x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.1% over 3 years.

own: Insiders own 11.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 53%.

That works out to $30K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.4M (8x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
